excerpt: Compare Business Bay and Dubai Marina rental investments by the actual unit, tenant access, service charges, net income and resale evidence.
introduction:
Business Bay and Dubai Marina offer different settings for a Dubai rental apartment, but neither neighbourhood guarantees a stronger return. The purchase price, building, access, tenant demand and owner costs of the exact unit determine the comparison. Use recent comparable leases and completed sales rather than relying only on an area-wide yield.

This guide sets out the checks and a sample calculation. The numbers form a worked example that can be adapted to the properties on your shortlist.
takeaways: Compare the building and intended tenant's daily routes as well as the area name.
Calculate net operating income after vacancy and owner expenses using the full acquisition cost.
Check service charges, short-term rental permissions if relevant, competing supply and exit costs.

sections.heading: How do the locations differ?
sections.body:
[Bayut's Business Bay guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/business-bay/) describes a mixed-use district around the Dubai Water Canal, with residential and commercial buildings. [Emaar's Dubai Marina guide](https://www.emaar.com/en/our-communities/dubai-marina) describes a waterfront residential setting with a promenade and retail. These are broad descriptions; the location and condition of a tower can change a tenant's experience.

The [RTA station map](https://www.rta.ae/wps/portal/rta/ae/public-transport/metro-stations-map) lists Business Bay and stations serving the Marina/JLT corridor. Check the actual walking route and transport service from the building; an area being on a map does not mean every apartment is close to a station.

Visit each candidate at the time its intended tenant might travel and inspect parking, noise, shared facilities and nearby services. The [JVC and Arjan area comparison](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) offers another example of building-level comparison.

sections.heading: Compare net income on the same basis
sections.body:
Suppose a sample Business Bay apartment costs AED 2,000,000 including acquisition costs and produces AED 90,000 annual net operating income after vacancy and owner expenses. Its net yield is 4.5%. A sample Marina apartment costs AED 2,200,000 and produces AED 99,000 net, also 4.5%. These example figures show how annual income and purchase costs affect the yield calculation.

The same percentage can conceal different cash requirements, income and risks. The Marina example requires AED 200,000 more capital and produces AED 9,000 more annual net income under these assumptions. The chart compares those sample income amounts before finance, tax and sale costs.

Use actual signed leases and unit-specific charges, then test a lower rent, longer vacancy and unexpected repair. The [Dubai net yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) explains the formula.

sections.heading: Check costs and building condition
sections.body:
Add the price, registration and brokerage, any finance charges, initial work and furnishing to calculate total acquisition cost. Ask for written quotes and confirm who pays each fee. Keep a reserve for a vacant period and repairs.

Use DLD's [service charge index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/service-charge-index/) and request the current statement for the unit. Check the approved rate, area basis, arrears and services included. Inspect the building's common areas and ask about maintenance history, management and any planned work.

Separate service charges from utilities, cooling and the cost of appointing a property manager. The [Dubai service-charge guide](/journal/dubai-apartment-service-charges-impact-on-rental-returns) shows how different charges affect income.

sections.heading: Which tenant and lease are you planning for?
sections.body:
For a long-term lease, compare recent signed rents for similar bedrooms, floor, condition, parking and furniture in the same building where possible. Record any rent-free period and how long the unit took to let. Compare asking rents with signed leases and the income collected from similar homes.

If considering a holiday home, verify the current permit, building rules and operator agreement with the relevant authority before making revenue assumptions. Budget for occupancy gaps, utilities, cleaning, platform and management costs. Short-term gross income is not directly comparable with a long-term rent without normalising expenses and time periods.

Test both the tenant's access and the unit's usability. A waterfront view or proximity to offices may be valuable to some occupants, but the premium depends on the property and actual evidence.

sections.heading: Assess future competition and exit
sections.body:
Review nearby projects and expected handovers alongside existing vacant or advertised units. A schedule may change, and a city-wide supply figure cannot establish what will happen in one building. Ask about the developer's progress and the local demand for the type of apartment you are considering.

Seek recent completed sales of comparable properties, noting the date, floor, condition and included parking. Separate asking prices from completed transactions. Include selling costs and any outstanding loan in a future cash calculation.

Compare projected yield with resale evidence, selling costs and your intended holding period. Make sure the investment remains manageable if the unit takes longer to let or sell.

sections.heading: Inspect how the investment will be managed
sections.body:
Ask who will arrange viewings, collect rent, manage the tenant relationship and coordinate repairs. If appointing a provider, check its licence and obtain a written agreement showing the fee basis, repair approval limits, reporting schedule and handling of funds. A building's common-area manager is not necessarily the manager of the individual tenancy.

Compare the time and cost involved if you manage the apartment yourself. Keep an allowance for maintenance inside the unit and ask how quickly essential repairs can be arranged when it is occupied. A convenient location cannot remove the need for a realistic operating plan. Revisit the calculation when a lease, service charge or management quote changes.

sections.heading: Compare current options
sections.body:
Browse [Aliyas Business Bay projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-business-bay) and [Dubai Marina projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-marina). Ask which specific units are currently available and request their plans, price, charges and terms. Compare each option using the same time period and assumptions.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget and intended lease strategy. Verify the property, current costs and applicable permissions before committing.
